source.title: Rethinking Circuit Completeness in Language Models: AND, OR, and ADDER Gates
source.authors: Hang Chen; Jiaying Zhu; Xin-Yu Yang; Wen-Ya Wang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests circuit faithfulness and completeness for GPT2-small IOI using intervention-based circuit discovery, but uses its own AND/OR/ADDER framework and does not reproduce the original IOI circuit-finding procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures the effects of removing gate edges and the behavior of GPT2-small IOI circuits after circuit removal. It also reports theoretical gate analyses, gate proportions and contribution plots, and results for GT and syntactic agreement; these are not separately rowed here because they do not directly measure the specified IOI claim or its listed versions. Only selected IOI circuit-removal settings are rowed; omissions are described below.
record.test_reason: This is a circuit-discovery methods paper. IOI on GPT2-small is its benchmark. It builds edge-level circuits with ACDC, EAP and EdgePruning under noising (Ns), denoising (Dn) and its own Ns+Dn framework. It then reports their completeness, faithfulness and gate properties. It never evaluates the Wang et al. 26-head circuit, its head classes, or its faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria. It does not ablate name movers to measure backup takeover, vary IOI prompts or models, or compare discovered circuits against the original. The circuit-removal tables (r10–r45) compare the paper's own method against baselines and Dn variants. The gate ablations (r1–r9) characterise the paper's AND/OR/ADDER decomposition, not any version's claim. The findings on dependence on intervention strategy and on backup-like OR edges are related but are not results on the IOI circuit itself. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that noising-only discovery misses OR-gate edges and so yields incomplete, run-variable circuits. They find that combining noising and denoising recovers all three gate types, improves removal-based completeness and lowers seed variability while keeping faithfulness. They report that OR gates link backup paths of the same function and AND gates join different necessary functions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates a combined noising/denoising circuit-discovery framework and compares ACDC, EAP, and EdgePruning. It does not reproduce the original IOI circuit’s extraction procedure or its exact 26-head circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported completeness outcomes vary with intervention strategy (Ns, Dn, Ns+Dn), discovery method (ACDC, EAP, EdgePruning), edge count, and metric (KL divergence versus task accuracy). The paper also reports that its Ns/Dn gate separation depends on matching circuit sizes; it assumes approximately equal edge counts for alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Removal-based completeness of automated GPT2-small IOI circuits depends on intervention direction. Ns circuits score lower than Ns+Dn or Dn at matched sizes; e.g. EAP 100 edges, KL 0.51 vs 0.74, accuracy after removal 0.74 vs 0.51. Results also vary with method and edge count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Completeness of noising-discovered IOI circuits is understated because noising misses OR-gate (redundant) edges.

fits_no_version.finding: Edge pairs in the discovered IOI circuits behave as AND, OR or ADDER gates under one- and two-edge ablation (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit edges combine via distinct logical relations, with OR edges redundant to each other.

fits_no_version.finding: In the ACDC IOI gate graphs, OR gates link same-function heads. Examples: S-inhibition heads fed by multiple induction heads; backup name movers fed by multiple S-inhibition heads. This is qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Redundant (backup) paths in the IOI circuit appear as OR gates among same-function heads.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The paper’s gate decomposition is inferred from the intersection of Ns and Dn circuits and assumes approximate granularity alignment; its reported optimal Ns:Dn edge ratios vary across methods and tasks. The authors note that XOR-like gates are not captured by their framework. The IOI evaluation is on GPT2-small and does not directly re-test the original 26-head circuit. This record samples only the 100- and 5000-edge IOI circuit-removal results.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix G Tables 7–8: omitted IOI circuit-removal results at 200, 500, 1000, and 2000 edges to keep the record selective; all methods and strategies are represented at 100 and 5000 edges. Figures 4, 5, and 9: omitted plotted summaries because selected exact IOI values are recorded from Tables 7–8. GT and syntactic-agreement circuit-removal results, Hamming-distance variability in Table 3, and gate contribution/proportion results in Appendices I–K were not included because they do not directly measure the listed IOI claim versions.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are never evaluated.
No name-mover ablation or measure of backup takeover.
Only GPT2-small. GT and SA circuits are not compared with IOI head roles.
Discovered circuits are never compared with the original circuit; mapping to IOI functions is only qualitative (Appendix I).
The ablation, metric and prompt sensitivity of the original IOI circuit's faithfulness and completeness are not measured.
No variation of name order, templates or number of names.

missing.what: Seed-to-seed Hamming-distance variability of IOI circuits, Ns vs Ns+Dn (e.g. EdgePruning 5000 edges 509.5±164.7)
Qualitative mapping of AND/OR/ADDER gate edges onto IOI head classes

record.verdict_notes: The study uses IOI only as a benchmark for its discovery framework. Row values in r1 and r4, and baselines in r10 and r12, are misread from Tables 5, 7 and 8. Table 5 has no per-method breakdown. Rows r10–r45 compare the paper's own method with others and should not bear on any version. The reader's V1/V4/V5 labels are dropped.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that the original 26-head circuit, its seven named head classes, or its specific faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are recovered. Its IOI graph study maps some discovered gate components to functions in the earlier IOI circuit, but it does not test the original circuit as a whole.
No experiment ablates the main name-mover heads and measures whether backup heads take over their role.

The paper uses GPT2-small and studies gate patterns on IOI, GT, and syntactic agreement; it does not test the same IOI head classes and roles in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or test reuse of the same components across tasks.

The paper compares circuit-discovery methods and noising/denoising strategies on IOI, but does not compare alternative circuit-finding methods against the original study’s exact circuit or test other ablation types beyond the strategies described.
The paper varies circuit-discovery method, intervention strategy, edge count, and evaluation metric. It does not test sensitivity to IOI prompt templates, name order, or other prompt distributions.
No evaluation varies IOI name order, templates, or number of names.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small IOI circuits discovered with ACDC, EAP, or EdgePruning; tested edge counts 100 and 5000
reader_labels.reason: The Ns circuits generally show weaker removal-based completeness than Ns+Dn, with differences varying by method and edge count; these are newly discovered circuits, not a direct test of the original 26-head circuit (r10-r33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small IOI circuits from ACDC, EAP, and EdgePruning under Ns, Dn, and Ns+Dn; edge counts 100 and 5000
reader_labels.reason: Removal-based completeness varies with discovery method and intervention strategy, rather than yielding an invariant result across choices (r10-r45).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small IOI, gate-edge removal and circuit-removal evaluations across the reported methods and selected edge counts
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports gate-specific effects and shows that measured completeness differs with intervention strategy, discovery method, edge count, and metric (r1-r9, r10-r45).
